ideas.pitch: A high-performance C++ dynamic routing daemon for edge mesh networks that self-heals dropped node topologies in real-time.
ideas.title: MeshRoute-C++: Dynamic Node Routing Optimizer
ideas.why_it_could_win: Directly targets the core hackathon theme of dynamic node routing and swarm network optimization, which will immediately appeal to C++ enthusiast judges evaluating low-level open source edge infrastructure.

ideas.pitch: An autonomous diagnostic agent running on constrained edge devices that detects network anomalies and triggers local self-healing routines.
ideas.title: SwarmTelemetry: Edge Node Diagnostics Agent
ideas.why_it_could_win: Mirrors winning autonomous operations patterns by solving real reliability pain points inherent in decentralized mesh topologies.

ideas.pitch: An open-source documentation generator tailored for C++ mesh protocol headers, automatically parsing packet structures and outputting live network topologies.
ideas.title: MeshDoc-Gen: Automated API & Protocol Documenter
ideas.why_it_could_win: Addresses documentation and testing tasks explicitly listed in the hackathon's scope, providing immense value to judges looking for robust open-source contributions.

ideas.pitch: A lightweight simulation harness for testing decentralized mesh routing protocols under simulated network partitions, high packet loss, and node latency.
ideas.title: EdgePacket-TestBed: Simulating High-Loss Mesh Environments
ideas.why_it_could_win: Solves testing challenges for edge protocol developers, fulfilling the hackathon's explicit focus on building robust edge infrastructure and testing suites.

ideas.pitch: A minimal consensus and state synchronization library designed for resource-constrained edge nodes operating over unreliable mesh links.
ideas.title: SwarmSync: Lightweight State Synchronization for Edge Swarms
ideas.why_it_could_win: Tackles hard engineering problems in distributed systems, matching winning patterns of high-difficulty technical execution.
